paragraphs.text: Then spake Jesus to the multitudes and to his disciples,
paragraphs.original: Τότε ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐλάλησεν τοῖς ὄχλοις καὶ τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ
paragraphs.translit: Tote ho Iēsous elalēsen tois ochlois kai tois mathētais autou

paragraphs.text: saying, The scribes and the Pharisees sit on Moses seat:
paragraphs.original: λέγων· Ἐπὶ τῆς Μωϋσέως καθέδρας ἐκάθισαν οἱ γραμματεῖς καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι.
paragraphs.translit: legōn· Epi tēs Mōyseōs kathedras ekathisan hoi grammateis kai hoi Pharisaioi.

paragraphs.text: all things therefore whatsoever they bid you, [these] do and observe: but do not ye after their works; for they say, and do not.
paragraphs.original: πάντα οὖν ὅσα ἐὰν εἴπωσιν ὑμῖν ποιήσατε καὶ τηρεῖτε, κατὰ δὲ τὰ ἔργα αὐτῶν μὴ ποιεῖτε, λέγουσιν γὰρ καὶ οὐ ποιοῦσιν.
paragraphs.translit: panta oun hosa ean eipōsin hymin poiēsate kai tēreite, kata de ta erga autōn mē poieite, legousin gar kai ou poiousin.

paragraphs.text: Yea, they bind heavy burdens and grievous to be borne, and lay them on men`s shoulders; but they themselves will not move them with their finger.
paragraphs.original: δεσμεύουσιν δὲ φορτία βαρέα καὶ ἐπιτιθέασιν ἐπὶ τοὺς ὤμους τῶν ἀνθρώπων, αὐτοὶ δὲ τῷ δακτύλῳ αὐτῶν οὐ θέλουσιν κινῆσαι αὐτά.
paragraphs.translit: desmeuousin de phortia barea kai epititheasin epi tous ōmous tōn anthrōpōn, autoi de tō daktylō autōn ou thelousin kinēsai auta.

paragraphs.text: But all their works they do to be seen of men: for they make broad their phylacteries, and enlarge the borders [of their garments],
paragraphs.original: πάντα δὲ τὰ ἔργα αὐτῶν ποιοῦσιν πρὸς τὸ θεαθῆναι τοῖς ἀνθρώποις· πλατύνουσι γὰρ τὰ φυλακτήρια αὐτῶν καὶ μεγαλύνουσι τὰ κράσπεδα,
paragraphs.translit: panta de ta erga autōn poiousin pros to theathēnai tois anthrōpois· platynousi gar ta phylaktēria autōn kai megalynousi ta kraspeda,

paragraphs.text: and love the chief place at feasts, and the chief seats in the synagogues,
paragraphs.original: φιλοῦσι δὲ τὴν πρωτοκλισίαν ἐν τοῖς δείπνοις καὶ τὰς πρωτοκαθεδρίας ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς
paragraphs.translit: philousi de tēn prōtoklisian en tois deipnois kai tas prōtokathedrias en tais synagōgais

paragraphs.text: and the salutations in the marketplaces, and to be called of men, Rabbi.
paragraphs.original: καὶ τοὺς ἀσπασμοὺς ἐν ταῖς ἀγοραῖς καὶ καλεῖσθαι ὑπὸ τῶν ἀνθρώπων· Ῥαββί.
paragraphs.translit: kai tous aspasmous en tais agorais kai kaleisthai hypo tōn anthrōpōn· Rhabbi.

paragraphs.text: But be not ye called Rabbi: for one is your teacher, and all ye are brethren.
paragraphs.original: ὑμεῖς δὲ μὴ κληθῆτε· Ῥαββί, εἷς γάρ ἐστιν ὑμῶν ὁ διδάσκαλος, πάντες δὲ ὑμεῖς ἀδελφοί ἐστε·
paragraphs.translit: hymeis de mē klēthēte· Rhabbi, heis gar estin hymōn ho didaskalos, pantes de hymeis adelphoi este·

paragraphs.text: And call no man your father on the earth: for one is your Father, [even] he who is in heaven.
paragraphs.original: καὶ πατέρα μὴ καλέσητε ὑμῶν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, εἷς γάρ ἐστιν ὑμῶν ὁ πατὴρ ὁ οὐράνιος·
paragraphs.translit: kai patera mē kalesēte hymōn epi tēs gēs, heis gar estin hymōn ho patēr ho ouranios·

paragraphs.text: Neither be ye called masters: for one is your master, [even] the Christ.
paragraphs.original: μηδὲ κληθῆτε καθηγηταί, ὅτι καθηγητὴς ὑμῶν ἐστιν εἷς ὁ χριστός·
paragraphs.translit: mēde klēthēte kathēgētai, hoti kathēgētēs hymōn estin heis ho christos·

paragraphs.text: But he that is greatest among you shall be your servant.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ μείζων ὑμῶν ἔσται ὑμῶν διάκονος.
paragraphs.translit: ho de meizōn hymōn estai hymōn diakonos.

paragraphs.text: And whosoever shall exalt himself shall be humbled; and whosoever shall humble himself shall be exalted.
paragraphs.original: ὅστις δὲ ὑψώσει ἑαυτὸν ταπεινωθήσεται, καὶ ὅστις ταπεινώσει ἑαυτὸν ὑψωθήσεται.
paragraphs.translit: hostis de hypsōsei heauton tapeinōthēsetai, kai hostis tapeinōsei heauton hypsōthēsetai.

paragraphs.text: But woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! because ye shut the kingdom of heaven against men: for ye enter not in yourselves, neither suffer ye them that are entering in to enter[.]
paragraphs.original: Οὐαὶ δὲ ὑμῖν, γραμματεῖς καὶ Φαρισαῖοι ὑποκριταί, ὅτι κλείετε τὴν βασιλείαν τῶν οὐρανῶν ἔμπροσθεν τῶν ἀνθρώπων· ὑμεῖς γὰρ οὐκ εἰσέρχεσθε, οὐδὲ τοὺς εἰσερχομένους ἀφίετε εἰσελθεῖν.
paragraphs.translit: Ouai de hymin, grammateis kai Pharisaioi hypokritai, hoti kleiete tēn basileian tōn ouranōn emprosthen tōn anthrōpōn· hymeis gar ouk eiserchesthe, oude tous eiserchomenous aphiete eiselthein.

paragraphs.text: Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye devour widows` houses, even while for a pretence ye make long prayers: therefore ye shall receive greater condemnation.
Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye compass sea and land to make one proselyte; and when he is become so, ye make him twofold more a son of hell than yourselves.
paragraphs.original: Οὐαὶ ὑμῖν, γραμματεῖς καὶ Φαρισαῖοι ὑποκριταί, ὅτι περιάγετε τὴν θάλασσαν καὶ τὴν ξηρὰν ποιῆσαι ἕνα προσήλυτον, καὶ ὅταν γένηται ποιεῖτε αὐτὸν υἱὸν γεέννης διπλότερον ὑμῶν.
paragraphs.translit: Ouai hymin, grammateis kai Pharisaioi hypokritai, hoti periagete tēn thalassan kai tēn xēran poiēsai hena prosēlyton, kai hotan genētai poieite auton hyion geennēs diploteron hymōn.

paragraphs.text: Woe unto you, ye blind guides, that say, Whosoever shall swear by the temple, it is nothing; but whosoever shall swear by the gold of the temple, he is a debtor.
paragraphs.original: Οὐαὶ ὑμῖν, ὁδηγοὶ τυφλοὶ οἱ λέγοντες· Ὃς ἂν ὀμόσῃ ἐν τῷ ναῷ, οὐδέν ἐστιν, ὃς δʼ ἂν ὀμόσῃ ἐν τῷ χρυσῷ τοῦ ναοῦ ὀφείλει.
paragraphs.translit: Ouai hymin, hodēgoi typhloi hoi legontes· Hos an omosē en tō naō, ouden estin, hos dʼ an omosē en tō chrysō tou naou opheilei.

paragraphs.text: Ye fools and blind: for which is greater, the gold, or the temple that hath sanctified the gold?
paragraphs.original: μωροὶ καὶ τυφλοί, τίς γὰρ μείζων ἐστίν, ὁ χρυσὸς ἢ ὁ ναὸς ὁ ἁγιάσας τὸν χρυσόν;
paragraphs.translit: mōroi kai typhloi, tis gar meizōn estin, ho chrysos ē ho naos ho hagiasas ton chryson;

paragraphs.text: And, Whosoever shall swear by the altar, it is nothing; but whosoever shall swear by the gift that is upon it, he is a debtor.
paragraphs.original: καί· Ὃς ἂν ὀμόσῃ ἐν τῷ θυσιαστηρίῳ, οὐδέν ἐστιν, ὃς δʼ ἂν ὀμόσῃ ἐν τῷ δώρῳ τῷ ἐπάνω αὐτοῦ ὀφείλει.
paragraphs.translit: kai· Hos an omosē en tō thysiastēriō, ouden estin, hos dʼ an omosē en tō dōrō tō epanō autou opheilei.

paragraphs.text: Ye blind: for which is greater, the gift, or the altar that sanctifieth the gift?
paragraphs.original: τυφλοί, τί γὰρ μεῖζον, τὸ δῶρον ἢ τὸ θυσιαστήριον τὸ ἁγιάζον τὸ δῶρον;
paragraphs.translit: typhloi, ti gar meizon, to dōron ē to thysiastērion to hagiazon to dōron;

paragraphs.text: He therefore that sweareth by the altar, sweareth by it, and by all things thereon.
paragraphs.original: ὁ οὖν ὀμόσας ἐν τῷ θυσιαστηρίῳ ὀμνύει ἐν αὐτῷ καὶ ἐν πᾶσι τοῖς ἐπάνω αὐτοῦ·
paragraphs.translit: ho oun omosas en tō thysiastēriō omnyei en autō kai en pasi tois epanō autou·

paragraphs.text: And he that sweareth by the temple, sweareth by it, and by him that dwelleth therein.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ὁ ὀμόσας ἐν τῷ ναῷ ὀμνύει ἐν αὐτῷ καὶ ἐν τῷ κατοικοῦντι αὐτόν·
paragraphs.translit: kai ho omosas en tō naō omnyei en autō kai en tō katoikounti auton·

paragraphs.text: And he that sweareth by the heaven, sweareth by the throne of God, and by him that sitteth thereon.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ὁ ὀμόσας ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ ὀμνύει ἐν τῷ θρόνῳ τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ ἐν τῷ καθημένῳ ἐπάνω αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: kai ho omosas en tō ouranō omnyei en tō thronō tou theou kai en tō kathēmenō epanō autou.

paragraphs.text: Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye tithe mint and anise and cummin, and have left undone the weightier matters of the law, justice, and mercy, and faith: but these ye ought to have done, and not to have left the other undone.
paragraphs.original: Οὐαὶ ὑμῖν, γραμματεῖς καὶ Φαρισαῖοι ὑποκριταί, ὅτι ἀποδεκατοῦτε τὸ ἡδύοσμον καὶ τὸ ἄνηθον καὶ τὸ κύμινον, καὶ ἀφήκατε τὰ βαρύτερα τοῦ νόμου, τὴν κρίσιν καὶ τὸ ἔλεος καὶ τὴν πίστιν· ταῦτα ἔδει ποιῆσαι κἀκεῖνα μὴ ἀφιέναι.
paragraphs.translit: Ouai hymin, grammateis kai Pharisaioi hypokritai, hoti apodekatoute to hēdyosmon kai to anēthon kai to kyminon, kai aphēkate ta barytera tou nomou, tēn krisin kai to eleos kai tēn pistin· tauta edei poiēsai kakeina mē aphienai.

paragraphs.text: Ye blind guides, that strain out the gnat, and swallow the camel!
paragraphs.original: ὁδηγοὶ τυφλοί, οἱ διϋλίζοντες τὸν κώνωπα τὴν δὲ κάμηλον καταπίνοντες.
paragraphs.translit: hodēgoi typhloi, hoi diylizontes ton kōnōpa tēn de kamēlon katapinontes.

paragraphs.text: Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye cleanse the outside of the cup and of the platter, but within they are full from extortion and excess.
paragraphs.original: Οὐαὶ ὑμῖν, γραμματεῖς καὶ Φαρισαῖοι ὑποκριταί, ὅτι καθαρίζετε τὸ ἔξωθεν τοῦ ποτηρίου καὶ τῆς παροψίδος, ἔσωθεν δὲ γέμουσιν ἐξ ἁρπαγῆς καὶ ἀκρασίας.
paragraphs.translit: Ouai hymin, grammateis kai Pharisaioi hypokritai, hoti katharizete to exōthen tou potēriou kai tēs paropsidos, esōthen de gemousin ex harpagēs kai akrasias.

paragraphs.text: Thou blind Pharisee, cleanse first the inside of the cup and of the platter, that the outside thereof may become clean also.
paragraphs.original: Φαρισαῖε τυφλέ, καθάρισον πρῶτον τὸ ἐντὸς τοῦ ποτηρίου καὶ τῆς παροψίδος, ἵνα γένηται καὶ τὸ ἐκτὸς αὐτοῦ καθαρόν.
paragraphs.translit: Pharisaie typhle, katharison prōton to entos tou potēriou kai tēs paropsidos, hina genētai kai to ektos autou katharon.

paragraphs.text: Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye are like unto whited sepulchres, which outwardly appear beautiful, but inwardly are full of dead men`s bones, and of all uncleanness.
paragraphs.original: Οὐαὶ ὑμῖν, γραμματεῖς καὶ Φαρισαῖοι ὑποκριταί, ὅτι παρομοιάζετε τάφοις κεκονιαμένοις, οἵτινες ἔξωθεν μὲν φαίνονται ὡραῖοι ἔσωθεν δὲ γέμουσιν ὀστέων νεκρῶν καὶ πάσης ἀκαθαρσίας·
paragraphs.translit: Ouai hymin, grammateis kai Pharisaioi hypokritai, hoti paromoiazete taphois kekoniamenois, hoitines exōthen men phainontai hōraioi esōthen de gemousin osteōn nekrōn kai pasēs akatharsias·

paragraphs.text: Even so ye also outwardly appear righteous unto men, but inwardly ye are full of hypocrisy and iniquity.
paragraphs.original: οὕτως καὶ ὑμεῖς ἔξωθεν μὲν φαίνεσθε τοῖς ἀνθρώποις δίκαιοι, ἔσωθεν δέ ἐστε μεστοὶ ὑποκρίσεως καὶ ἀνομίας.
paragraphs.translit: houtōs kai hymeis exōthen men phainesthe tois anthrōpois dikaioi, esōthen de este mestoi hypokriseōs kai anomias.

paragraphs.text: Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye build the sepulchres of the prophets, and garnish the tombs of the righteous,
paragraphs.original: Οὐαὶ ὑμῖν, γραμματεῖς καὶ Φαρισαῖοι ὑποκριταί, ὅτι οἰκοδομεῖτε τοὺς τάφους τῶν προφητῶν καὶ κοσμεῖτε τὰ μνημεῖα τῶν δικαίων,
paragraphs.translit: Ouai hymin, grammateis kai Pharisaioi hypokritai, hoti oikodomeite tous taphous tōn prophētōn kai kosmeite ta mnēmeia tōn dikaiōn,

paragraphs.text: and say, If we had been in the days of our fathers, we should not have been partakers with them in the blood of the prophets.
paragraphs.original: καὶ λέγετε· Εἰ ἤμεθα ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις τῶν πατέρων ἡμῶν, οὐκ ἂν ἤμεθα αὐτῶν κοινωνοὶ ἐν τῷ αἵματι τῶν προφητῶν·
paragraphs.translit: kai legete· Ei ēmetha en tais hēmerais tōn paterōn hēmōn, ouk an ēmetha autōn koinōnoi en tō haimati tōn prophētōn·

paragraphs.text: Wherefore ye witness to yourselves, that ye are sons of them that slew the prophets.
paragraphs.original: ὥστε μαρτυρεῖτε ἑαυτοῖς ὅτι υἱοί ἐστε τῶν φονευσάντων τοὺς προφήτας.
paragraphs.translit: hōste martyreite heautois hoti hyioi este tōn phoneusantōn tous prophētas.

paragraphs.text: Fill ye up then the measure of your fathers.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ὑμεῖς πληρώσατε τὸ μέτρον τῶν πατέρων ὑμῶν.
paragraphs.translit: kai hymeis plērōsate to metron tōn paterōn hymōn.

paragraphs.text: Ye serpents, ye offspring of vipers, how shall ye escape the judgment of hell?
paragraphs.original: ὄφεις γεννήματα ἐχιδνῶν, πῶς φύγητε ἀπὸ τῆς κρίσεως τῆς γεέννης;
paragraphs.translit: opheis gennēmata echidnōn, pōs phygēte apo tēs kriseōs tēs geennēs;

paragraphs.text: Therefore, behold, I send unto you prophets, and wise men, and scribes: some of them shall ye kill and crucify; and some of them shall ye scourge in your synagogues, and persecute from city to city:
paragraphs.original: διὰ τοῦτο ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ ἀποστέλλω πρὸς ὑμᾶς προφήτας καὶ σοφοὺς καὶ γραμματεῖς· ἐξ αὐτῶν ἀποκτενεῖτε καὶ σταυρώσετε, καὶ ἐξ αὐτῶν μαστιγώσετε ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς ὑμῶν καὶ διώξετε ἀπὸ πόλεως εἰς πόλιν·
paragraphs.translit: dia touto idou egō apostellō pros hymas prophētas kai sophous kai grammateis· ex autōn apokteneite kai staurōsete, kai ex autōn mastigōsete en tais synagōgais hymōn kai diōxete apo poleōs eis polin·

paragraphs.text: that upon you may come all the righteous blood shed on the earth, from the blood of Abel the righteous unto the blood of Zachariah son of Barachiah, whom ye slew between the sanctuary and the altar.
paragraphs.original: ὅπως ἔλθῃ ἐφʼ ὑμᾶς πᾶν αἷμα δίκαιον ἐκχυννόμενον ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἀπὸ τοῦ αἵματος Ἅβελ τοῦ δικαίου ἕως τοῦ αἵματος Ζαχαρίου υἱοῦ Βαραχίου, ὃν ἐφονεύσατε μεταξὺ τοῦ ναοῦ καὶ τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου.
paragraphs.translit: hopōs elthē ephʼ hymas pan haima dikaion ekchynnomenon epi tēs gēs apo tou haimatos Habel tou dikaiou heōs tou haimatos Zachariou hyiou Barachiou, hon ephoneusate metaxy tou naou kai tou thysiastēriou.

paragraphs.text: Verily I say unto you, All these things shall come upon this generation.
paragraphs.original: ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ἥξει ταῦτα πάντα ἐπὶ τὴν γενεὰν ταύτην.
paragraphs.translit: amēn legō hymin, hēxei tauta panta epi tēn genean tautēn.

paragraphs.text: O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, that killeth the prophets, and stoneth them that are sent unto her! how often would I have gathered thy children together, even as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings, and ye would not!
paragraphs.original: Ἰερουσαλὴμ Ἰερουσαλήμ, ἡ ἀποκτείνουσα τοὺς προφήτας καὶ λιθοβολοῦσα τοὺς ἀπεσταλμένους πρὸς αὐτήν— ποσάκις ἠθέλησα ἐπισυναγαγεῖν τὰ τέκνα σου, ὃν τρόπον ὄρνις ἐπισυνάγει τὰ νοσσία αὐτῆς ὑπὸ τὰς πτέρυγας, καὶ οὐκ ἠθελήσατε;
paragraphs.translit: Ierousalēm Ierousalēm, hē apokteinousa tous prophētas kai lithobolousa tous apestalmenous pros autēn— posakis ēthelēsa episynagagein ta tekna sou, hon tropon ornis episynagei ta nossia autēs hypo tas pterygas, kai ouk ēthelēsate;

paragraphs.text: Behold, your house is left unto you desolate.
paragraphs.original: ἰδοὺ ἀφίεται ὑμῖν ὁ οἶκος ὑμῶν ἔρημος.
paragraphs.translit: idou aphietai hymin ho oikos hymōn erēmos.

paragraphs.text: For I say unto you, Ye shall not see me henceforth, till ye shall say, Blessed [is] he that cometh in the name of the Lord.
paragraphs.original: λέγω γὰρ ὑμῖν, οὐ μή με ἴδητε ἀπʼ ἄρτι ἕως ἂν εἴπητε· Εὐλογημένος ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἐν ὀνόματι κυρίου.
paragraphs.translit: legō gar hymin, ou mē me idēte apʼ arti heōs an eipēte· Eulogēmenos ho erchomenos en onomati kyriou.
